c: THE PAGE. All four axes at once — collection.tabs over subtopics, a different composition inside each, views.tabs over two representations of one object, media geometry resolving the subdesign, and unrestricted page scroll. Desktop, tablet and phone.
THE DEFAULT. A short task, a rule, then the reasoning at a controlled measure. The unused width to the right is reading margin.
ADVERSARIAL — seven steps. The step count does not change the composition; the page is taller.
A prompt that carries substantial information, beside the reasoning. Chosen by the author, never inferred.
ADVERSARIAL — a one-line prompt in a split. The author asked for a split, so it is a split.
Two cases whose relationship matters, then why they agree.
ADVERSARIAL — cases of very unequal length. Their heights are not consulted.

visual.side — a portrait figure and the reading of it. The tablet render is the one to look at: the switch point is derived from the plane's own width, so it stacks rather than setting prose in a 314px column.
ADVERSARIAL — a wide figure resolves visual.down. Same authored composition, the other approved subdesign; no state change at any width.
The cases across, then ONE visual belonging to both. A balanced figure resolves comparison.sharedVisual.side.
ADVERSARIAL — a wide figure resolves comparison.sharedVisual.down. BOTH REMAIN comparison.sharedVisual: a subdesign change with no semantic change.
COLLECTION · repeat — several sibling items, all visible. repeat(single.flow), and each child literally IS a single.flow, measures included.
ADVERSARIAL — six examples, one of a single step and one of three. The count is nowhere in the geometry.
COLLECTION · tabs — SEVERAL SIBLING ITEMS; SELECT ONE. Three different examples, rendered as an item selector. An authored choice about a Worked Examples page, not a response to height.
ADVERSARIAL — an eight-step example beside a one-step one. Length is not a reason to add a tab, and not a reason to remove one.

VIEWS · tabs — ONE OBJECT, SEEN SEVERAL WAYS, rendered as a view switch. This is what visualCheck was: views.tabs{ Workings → single.flow, Graph check → visual }. There is no visualCheck rendering logic anywhere.
ADVERSARIAL — a line of mathematics wider than its measure, inside a view. It overflows locally; the view switch is untouched.
SCROLL · y = page. The default. Nothing bounded, nothing hidden, nothing compressed — several screens tall, and that is the outcome rather than a failure.
SCROLL · y = pane. An explicit template feature, not a renderer trick: the stimulus stays while the worklist moves. The narrow state gives the bound up and returns to page scroll.
SCROLL · x = local-when-needed. A table of values and an un-breakable expansion. Each overflows inside its own region; the page never scrolls sideways.
